lines.text: How does your phone know it's your face, and not your twin's?
You glance at it, and it just opens.
Behind that glance, your phone does four jobs. Let's follow your face.
Step one. The dots. The moment you look, the camera at the top fires thousands of invisible dots at your face.
They're infrared light. Your eyes can't see them, but the camera can. It works even in total darkness.
Step two. The depth map. Each dot lands at a different distance. Your nose is closer. Your eyes sit deeper.
From where the dots land, the phone builds a 3D shape of your face. A depth map.
That's why a photo can't fool it. A photo is flat. Your face isn't.
Step three. The math. Your phone never stores a picture of your face.
A neural network turns that depth map into a long list of numbers. Your face, as math.
That math is locked inside a protected part of the chip, called the Secure Enclave. It never leaves your phone.
Step four. The match. Every unlock, your face becomes new math, and it's compared with the math you saved.
Close enough? Unlocked. Not close enough? Try again. Five misses, and it asks for your passcode.
It also wants your passcode after a restart, or if nobody has unlocked it for two days.
So if it's comparing shapes, what happens when two faces have the same shape?
Quick thing. How AI like this works is part of the AI track on Teyro.
Okay. Back to the twins.
First, the tricks that don't work. Hold up a photo? Flat. Rejected.
A mask? A second neural network is trained just to catch fakes.
Eyes closed? It checks you're actually looking. Grow a beard? It slowly learns your new face.
Now, the twin. Apple says a random stranger has less than a one in a million chance of unlocking your phone. That's with one saved face.
But Apple also says that chance is higher for twins and siblings who look like you, and for kids under thirteen.
Their faces really can be that close. So if you have a lookalike twin, Apple recommends using a passcode.
So. Thousands of dots. A depth map. Your face as math. A match, every time. And your twin is the one weak spot.
Your phone doesn't see your face. It measures it.
